title: State the exact OM14 proposition and answer boundary
author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: The 1.3.0 release records OM14 as a legacy scope label without a rule-linked supporting claim, and the six-entry catalog has no Easy Ontology comparison.
proposedBehavior: Publish the exact scoped claim and its source-linked comparison in new immutable artifacts; preserve all historical releases and item revisions.
rationale: The existing Full-route OM14 items directly ask about conceptual and empirical criteria versus a further metaphysical test. A scoped comparison can use that interpreted proposition without guessing from ordinary-object realism.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: Some existence questions can be settled by a concept’s ordinary application conditions together with relevant empirical facts, without an additional distinctively metaphysical existence test.
neighboringViews: Denial of a further test for unrelated reasons
nonEntailments: This method is compatible with realism
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: The rule’s legacy scope is not an exact reviewed proposition and its two positive items are related in wording.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: The breadth and realism compatibility of Easy Ontology are disputed; this rule remains limited to the question wording.

sourceClaims.claim: Marschall describes Easy Ontology as settling many ontological questions through conceptual truths and empirical knowledge, while disputing whether its defense of realism succeeds.

alternatives: Add the entire draft question pool: rejected because the existing OM14 items ask this narrow method directly.
Infer the method from ordinary-object realism: rejected because belief in objects does not settle metaontological method.
Retain an unqualified identity label: rejected because the pilot asks only a limited proposition.
respondentImpact: Full-route respondents may see a limited Easy Ontology comparison when OM14 evidence is settled; Quick and Standard leave its defining criterion unmeasured. No raw answer or threshold changes.
historicalCompatibility: The 1.3.0 model, six-entry catalog, route items, source ledger, and original results remain byte-identical. A new manifest pins the new model and catalog; old administrations replay under their recorded versions.

approvals.note: Reviewed the exact scoped claim, neighboring realism and nominalism positions, and source limits.
Reviewed historical version binding, route opportunity, and adversarial software fixtures.

release.migration: No raw-response migration. Historical model and affinity results retain their previous manifest; new administrations use the new tuple.
